name: Dining Room
description: A room whose entire dimension is set by one object and the act of sitting round it. Everything else — the sideboard wall, the door position, the window that must not be behind the host's head — follows from a table and the ability to walk behind a pushed-back chair. It is the most rigidly dimensioned room in the house and the one most often drawn a foot too small.

history.replaced: the hall, where the household had eaten at a board set up and taken down
history.note: A dedicated eating room is a Georgian invention and a class marker: it requires enough furniture to leave a table standing permanently, and enough servants to carry food a distance from the kitchen. Robert Kerr in 1864 could still assume separate dining and drawing rooms as the minimum of gentility. The room survived the servants by a century, then lost to the open plan — but it has not died, because the one thing an open plan cannot supply is a room you can shut for three hours.

dimensions.critical_dimension: The short dimension. A table for eight is 40 in wide; a chair pushed back needs 36 in; passing behind it needs another 18 in. That is 40 + 2(36) + 2(18) = 148 in, so 12 ft 4 in is the absolute floor and 13 ft is the working minimum. A 12 ft dining room is a fault dressed as a room, and it is the commonest dimensional error in production housing.

furniture.note: 36 in chair pull plus 18 in passage. Seats 10 at 40 x 120.
Needs an uninterrupted wall of at least 6 ft. This is what the second window usually kills.

daylight.orientation: East or south-east for a breakfast-doubling room; west where the room is used at night and the low sun is wanted on the table. Avoid a window directly behind the head of the table.
daylight.note: A dining room is used more by candle and lamp than by daylight, which is why it tolerates a deeper plan position than a parlor and why its lighting slot matters more than its glazing.

must_adjoin.why: Food and china must arrive without crossing a public room. Where there is no pantry the kitchen takes its place and the door position becomes critical.

should_adjoin.why: Guests reach it without passing through another room, which is what makes it a formal room rather than a back room.
The withdrawing sequence: dine, then withdraw. Doors aligned where the two are used together.

must_not_adjoin.why: A lavatory door opening into or directly visible from a dining room is the single most avoidable plan error of the last forty years.
Noise and smell during the one meal the room exists for.

servicing.ventilation: Cross ventilation preferred; a room of eight people at dinner is a real thermal load.
servicing.heat: Historically a fireplace on the interior wall opposite the sideboard.
servicing.electrical: One switched central outlet on a dimmer at the table centre, and the table centre is set by the room, not by the framing.

style_variation.note: Often the most elaborately trimmed room in the house, above the parlour, because it is where guests sit longest and looking at the cornice.
Frequently the oval or apsidal-ended room where Adamesque planning shows off.
Plate rail, built-in sideboard and a beamed ceiling; the built-in replaces the freestanding sideboard, which changes the wall requirement entirely.
Reduced to a dining ell off the living room, often with no door and no defensible wall for a sideboard.
Usually present as a formal room the household does not use, which is a programming failure rather than an architectural one — ask the client how many times a year before drawing it.

code.requirement: Habitable room, minimum 7 ft in any horizontal dimension and 70 sf
code.conflict: The code minimum is less than half the furniture minimum. A code-compliant dining room can be unusable, which is the clearest case in the house of a floor mistaken for a target.

sources: Cromley, The Food Axis: Cooking, Eating and the Architecture of American Houses
Panero and Zelnik, Human Dimension and Interior Space
